relevance_reason: Reports EBS patients with biallelic DST mutations, including two novel variants, and reviews the literature on DST-associated EBS (EBS3).

findings.statement: Ganani et al. (2021) used whole-exome and direct sequencing to identify biallelic DST mutations in 5 patients with epidermolysis bullosa simplex from 3 families. Two of the variants had not been reported before: c.7097dupA (p.Tyr2366X) and c.7429delC (p.Leu2477Serfs*13).
quotes: Mutation analysis revealed DST mutations in five patients belonging to three families. Two variants have not been previously reported: c.7097dupA (p.Tyr2366X) and c.7429delC (p.Leu2477Serfs*13).
Whole-exome and direct sequencing were used for variant analysis.

findings.statement: Ganani et al. (2021) reviewed 6 previously reported cases, bringing the total number of individuals with EBS due to DST variants to 11. They noted that patients displayed distinctive phenotypes regardless of the causative variant.
quotes: We identified an additional six cases in the literature, bringing the total number of individuals affected with EBS due to DST variants to 11. Patients displayed distinctive phenotypes regardless of the causative variant.

findings.statement: Ganani et al. (2021) stated that DST-associated EBS is transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait and is caused by mutations in DST, which encodes an epithelial isoform of dystonin.
quotes: DST-associated EBS is transmitted as an autosomal recessive trait.
a minority of affected individuals carry mutations in non-keratin genes including DST encoding an epithelial isoform of dystonin

relevance_reason: The title reports autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex caused by loss of BPAG1-e (BP230) expression, which is the subject of this entry. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Liu et al. (2012) reported autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex caused by loss of BPAG1-e expression.
quotes: Autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to loss of BPAG1-e expression.

relevance_reason: First report of a homozygous DST nonsense mutation affecting BPAG1-e causing autosomal recessive EBS with BP230 deficiency.

findings.statement: Groves et al. (2010) reported a 38-year-old man with an inherited skin fragility disorder who had lifelong generalized trauma-induced spontaneous blisters and erosions, particularly around the ankles. From age 37 years he experienced episodic numbness in his limbs; he also had a concomitant diagnosis of CADASIL, which the authors noted complicated interpretation of whether the neurologic symptoms were due to the DST mutation.
quotes: The 38-year-old affected individual has lifelong generalized trauma-induced spontaneous blisters and erosions, particularly around the ankles.
In addition, he experiences episodic numbness in his limbs, which started at the age of 37 years.

although he has a concomitant diagnosis of CADASIL (cerebral arteriopathy, autosomal dominant, with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy), a cerebral small-vessel arteriopathy, which thus complicates the genotype-phenotype interpretation

findings.statement: In a 38-year-old man with autosomal recessive epidermolysis bullosa simplex, Groves et al. (2010) identified a homozygous nonsense mutation, p.Gln1124X, in the DST gene within the region encoding the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform BPAG1-e (BP230). The authors concluded that BPAG1-e pathology underlies a new form of autosomal recessive EBS.
quotes: We now report an inherited skin fragility disorder with a homozygous nonsense mutation in the dystonin gene (DST) that encodes the coiled-coil domain of the epithelial isoform of bullous pemphigoid antigen 1, BPAG1-e (also known as BP230).
the clinicopathological findings expand the molecular basis of EB by identifying BPAG1-e pathology in a new form of autosomal recessive EB simplex

findings.statement: Groves et al. (2010) found that the DST p.Gln1124X mutation led to loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques and complete absence of skin immunostaining for BPAG1-e, with reduced labeling for plectin, beta-4 integrin, and type XVII collagen.
quotes: The mutation, p.Gln1124X, leads to the loss of hemidesmosomal inner plaques and a complete absence of skin immunostaining for BPAG1-e, as well as reduced labeling for plectin, the beta4 integrin subunit, and for type XVII collagen.
